title: I Used the Miso-Crock Shelf Hours on the Chair Who Took My Numbered Weight

parts.text: I stepped into the crock shelf at 10:08 a.m. and chair Yuki was already using numbered gear. The board said: ONE CROCK. THIRTY MINUTES. WEIGHTS STAY WITH THE SLOT. I was thirty-three, kitchen secretary, holding a checkout that listed our numbered weight. Yuki shrugged. "Chairs are the koji." I photographed the board, the booking, and her leftover drop-lid on my numbered weight. Then I asked for the crock log. At 10:16 the shelf pinged why Yuki's name was on my lid. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. A paper policy is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The shelf can see Yuki's leftover drop-lid on my numbered weight.

social.video_title: She took my numbered miso weight on my crock — Part 1/2
social.description: Crock shelf, leftover drop-lid, a thirty-minute clock she posted. I logged the weight. Would you have asked for the crock log?

parts.text: Yuki called it burping until the shelf asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the board, and the lid still. The weight went back to my numbered slot. Yuki ran a slot of her own and told the next chair atmosphere was always about optics. Optics is a word people use when a booking exists. Policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT THE KOJI. I keep my weight on a labeled peg. Yuki brown-bags her burping. The shelf finally looks like a slot, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Crock log, numbered weight, and a second line on the board. Was burping ever my lid?
